name: ThermGAS (formerly Thermal Gas Systems)
industry_focus: Refrigerant and specialty-gas leak monitoring (mechanical rooms, data centers, semiconductor, battery manufacturing)
us_presence: U.S. headquarters and manufacturer; notable-installations list names organizations across North America (company claim, refrigerant applications).
battery_experience: Published DMC application note (2026) and battery webpage; no public battery-plant customer reference found.
rationale: Sponsor. PAIR fixed monitors marketed for DMC vapor monitoring in Li-ion battery manufacturing.

name: ION Science
hq: Royston (Fowlmere), UK; U.S. office Stafford, TX
industry_focus: Photoionization (PID) VOC detection - portable, personal and fixed
us_presence: ION Science Inc. office (4153 Bluebonnet Dr, Stafford, TX 77477). Official Where-to-Buy page tags U.S. distributors in CT, IL, FL, UT, NJ, GA, TX, CA, LA, MA (company-to-state pairing not machine-readable; to be confirmed).
battery_experience: FALCO 2 11.7 lists 'Li-ion Battery Manufacturing and Storage' among typical applications; publishes DMC response factors (11.7 eV RF 1.50; 10.6 eV RF 60).
relationship: Closest direct competitor: fixed DMC-capable VOC monitor explicitly marketed to Li-ion battery manufacturing.
rationale: Same task (fixed continuous vapor monitoring in battery plants); different technology (PID, non-selective).

name: Riken Keiki (U.S.: RKI Instruments)
hq: Tokyo, Japan (Riken Keiki); U.S. subsidiary RKI Instruments, Union City, CA
industry_focus: Industrial fixed and portable gas detection
relevant_products: SD-D58 (hot-wire, pump suction); SD-1RI (NDIR, diffusion); SD-1GP / SD-1GH (diffusion); GADMS Lite remote monitoring
us_presence: RKI Instruments office in Union City, CA (verified on RKI site). PK Safety (CA) is RKI's #1 distributor and factory-authorized service center (verified); AFC International (DeMotte, IN) is a large RKI distributor (Inferred, search excerpt). Full U.S. distributor list not published.
battery_experience: Official Riken Keiki battery page: electrolyte-filling monitors for DMC/EMC/DEC; >10,000 detectors operating at Li-ion production sites worldwide; 20+ years in Li-ion; case study of a ppm-level range customised for an electrolyte-filling customer. Also NMP duct monitors (SD-2500/2600), testing (GD-70D) and separator (FI-900).
relationship: Direct competitor with the broadest battery-process portfolio (drying, filling, testing, separator). DMC-specific detection limits not published.
rationale: Official product page names the same task (electrolyte filling) and the same solvents. RKI (Union City, CA) is the U.S. channel; PK Safety (CA) is an authorized service center.

name: Honeywell (Li-ion Tamer; RAEGuard 2 PID)
hq: USA (corporate HQ not re-verified in this session)
industry_focus: Building automation, fire/life safety, industrial gas detection
relevant_products: Li-ion Tamer (Gen2+/Gen3) off-gas sensors; RAEGuard 2 PID
us_presence: Products sold in U.S. via Honeywell Building Automation and resellers (e.g., Instrumart list price). Li-ion Tamer Gen2+ holds a California State Fire Marshal listing (Jan 2025).
battery_experience: Li-ion Tamer acquired from Nexceris (July 2025); detects electrolyte solvent vapor off-gas events in battery racks/ESS; UL 2075 recognition for electrolyte solvent vapor (DEC, DMC, EMC) reported. Honeywell markets an integrated "Gigafactory Fire Solution" built around Li-ion Tamer Gen 3 + VESDA for battery production plants (S38, S43). Public U.S. reference: Alamitos Energy Center BESS, Long Beach CA (S39).
relationship: Event detection (cell venting) rather than DMC concentration monitoring; strong brand and fire-system channel.
rationale: Different measurement (rate-of-change off-gas event, FM 6540 approved) but competes for the same gigafactory safety budget. Conflict: Gen 3 product page marked Discontinued while the Gen 3 data sheet and gigafactory page remain current - unresolved.

name: Cubic Sensor and Instrument Co., Ltd.
hq: Wuhan, China; North American JV 'Cubic Innovaer' (Dec 2025, location not stated)
industry_focus: Gas sensor modules (NDIR, ultrasonic) and analyzers for OEMs
us_presence: North American JV Cubic Innovaer announced Dec 2025; no verified U.S. office address or distributor found.
battery_experience: ATRS-1050 designed for DMC/EMC/EC vapor detection for thermal runaway and battery manufacturing leak detection (catalog).
relationship: OEM component sensor; DMC-specific NDIR but at high-ppm scale (0-10,000 ppm; +/-200 ppm in 0-2,000 ppm).
rationale: Detects DMC but resolution suits leak/thermal-runaway events, not low-ppm trace monitoring. Could be integrated by system builders as a low-cost alternative.

name: NevadaNano (Nevada Nanotech Systems, Inc.)
industry_focus: MEMS 'Molecular Property Spectrometer' (MPS) gas sensors for flammable gas and refrigerants
relevant_products: MPS Flammable Gas Sensor (H2 + DMC + EMC classification)
us_presence: U.S. headquarters in Nevada; sells sensors to OEMs.
battery_experience: Markets DMC/EMC classification for BESS off-gas early warning; no field calibration, 15-year sensor life (vendor claim).
relationship: Component supplier for BESS/battery-safety devices; adjacent to factory DMC monitoring.
rationale: DMC-capable but positioned for BESS enclosures; no concentration/LOD spec for DMC published on page read.

name: Infrasensing
industry_focus: Environmental monitoring sensors for data centers / critical facilities
us_presence: Sold 'through OEM partners in select markets'; no U.S. office verified.
battery_experience: Detects DMC, DEC, EMC off-gas in stationary Li-ion/BESS racks; calibration-free; UL 61010 recognized; explicitly 'not a fire detection or life safety system'.
relationship: Rack-level BESS/data-center off-gas monitoring; overlaps ThermGAS's data-center audience, not factory DMC.
rationale: Adjacent customer segment (data centers) where ThermGAS also sells refrigerant monitors.

name: MSA Safety (incl. Bacharach)
hq: USA (HQ not re-verified in this session)
industry_focus: Safety products incl. fixed gas detection; HVAC-R leak detection via Bacharach (acquired July 2021, $337M)
relevant_products: Chillgard 5000 (PAIR refrigerant monitor); Bacharach MGS-400 series; Bacharach Multi-Zone
us_presence: U.S. company with national distribution (details not collected).
battery_experience: None found for DMC. Chillgard 5000 gas list is refrigerants only.
relationship: Uses the same PAIR principle (1 ppm refrigerants) - the most credible technology peer if it chose to configure for DMC; main rival in ThermGAS's core refrigerant market.
rationale: Not a DMC competitor today; strategic threat in core business and potential entrant.

name: Gasmet Technologies (a Nederman company)
hq: Vantaa, Finland; North American entity Mississauga, ON, Canada
industry_focus: FTIR multi-gas analyzers (emissions, process, safety, portable)
relevant_products: GT6000 Mobilis with GAS-LIB-BTRY Li-ion battery library
us_presence: Sold via U.S. distributors/rental houses (e.g., Advanced Test Equipment Corp., San Diego CA); no U.S. office verified.
battery_experience: Fixed Li-ion battery library includes DMC, EMC, EC, DEC, HF, CO, H2-related species (dated 2025-11-14).
relationship: Multi-component FTIR used for battery off-gas / abuse testing; could substitute for area monitoring at higher cost/complexity.
rationale: DMC capability verified in library; positioned for testing/analysis rather than permanent area alarms.

name: INFICON
hq: Bad Ragaz, Switzerland (Inferred); U.S. office East Syracuse, NY
industry_focus: Leak detection, vacuum and gas analysis instruments
us_presence: U.S. office in East Syracuse, NY; rental via Advanced Test Equipment Corp. (CA).
battery_experience: End-of-line leak testing of pouch/prismatic/round/coin cells; quadrupole MS detects electrolyte solvents; 1e-6 mbar.l/s helium-equivalent; 'E-Check (DMC)' accessory listed.
relationship: Cell-level QC substitute: catches leaking cells before they reach storage/aging areas, reducing the need for ambient alarms; does not monitor room air.
rationale: Different task (product leak test) but addresses the same root cause (electrolyte leakage).
